title: 23-Year-Old Punjab-Origin Man Shot Dead in Targeted Attack Near Vancouver
excerpt: The Langley resident was found with gunshot wounds in a business-complex parking lot on October 5; a torched getaway car was recovered nearby, and homicide investigators say the attack appears targeted.
body:
• A 23-year-old Punjab-origin man was shot dead on October 5 in the parking lot of a business complex in Langley, British Columbia, near Vancouver. He died at the scene despite life-saving efforts.
  • Langley RCMP found him with gunshot wounds around 9:45 pm in the 6000-block of 200 Street; about 20 minutes later, a burnt sedan believed to have been used in the shooting was found near 232 Street and 75 Avenue.
  • The Integrated Homicide Investigation Team has taken over the case, says preliminary information indicates the shooting was targeted, and is seeking witnesses and dashcam footage from 8:30–10:30 pm on October 5.
  • The victim's identity has been withheld as the investigation continues; police have not ruled out a link to gang violence, which has claimed a series of young Punjabi lives in the Lower Mainland in recent years.

A targeted killing in Langley

A 23-year-old Punjab-origin man was shot dead in Langley, a city near Vancouver in British Columbia, in what police believe was a targeted attack, according to The Tribune. The shooting occurred on October 5, and the victim — a Langley resident — died at the scene.

https://x.com/thetribunechd/status/2108029182114771100

Around 9:45 pm, Langley RCMP responded to reports of a shooting in the 6000-block of 200 Street. Officers found the young man suffering from gunshot wounds in the parking lot of a business complex. Despite life-saving efforts by first responders, he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Roughly 20 minutes later, police received a report of a vehicle fire near the 232 Street and 75 Avenue area. A burnt sedan was recovered and is believed to have been used in the shooting, the Tribune reported. Criminals often torch getaway vehicles after a major crime to destroy evidence, a pattern familiar to investigators in the region.

IHIT takes the lead

Two days after the incident, the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT) of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police took over the investigation, working alongside the Langley RCMP, the Integrated Forensic Identification Services and the BC Coroners Service.

"This investigation is in its early stages, and it is essential for investigators to establish a timeline of events leading up to the shooting."

— Sergeant Freda Fong, Integrated Homicide Investigation Team

Sergeant Freda Fong of the IHIT said investigators are conducting an extended canvass for witnesses and video at both the shooting and arson scenes. The team has appealed to anyone who was in the area between 8:30 pm and 10:30 pm on October 5 to come forward, and is specifically seeking dashcam footage.

While the motive remains under investigation, preliminary information indicates the incident was targeted, police said. The RCMP has withheld the victim's identity while the investigation is underway.

A familiar pattern in the Lower Mainland

The killing fits a grim pattern. Young men of Punjabi origin have been disproportionately represented among gang-linked homicide victims in British Columbia's Lower Mainland for years, a trend that has prompted repeated interventions by community leaders and law enforcement. The Tribune noted that the killing could be linked to a gang war, though investigators have not confirmed that publicly.

For the large Punjabi diaspora in the Vancouver area — one of the biggest Sikh and Punjabi communities outside India — each such killing reverberates through families who migrated for safety and opportunity. Community organisations in Surrey and Langley have in recent years run outreach programmes aimed at steering young men away from gang recruitment.

What happens next

IHIT investigators will now reconstruct the victim's movements in the hours before the shooting, trace the burnt sedan's ownership history, and work through forensic evidence from both scenes. Anyone with information about the shooting or the vehicle fire is asked to contact the IHIT tip line. Until arrests are made, the case remains in its earliest stages — and the community waits for answers.
